correctness.rationale: The expansion on the tangent hyperplane gives the cone criterion Av proportional to Aᵗv^[4]; rescaling normalizes it uniquely up to F4*. Invertibility gives smoothness and, on a normalized isotropic line, the two-sided tangent radical is precisely that line, so the quotient plane cubic is smooth. The affine equations v_i^4−(Cv)_i have disjoint leading monomials in a graded order and invertible Jacobian C, so have exactly 4^5 reduced roots over the closure. Iteration bounds the field by F_{2^{2h}} for h the order of C. Our independent binary-RREF enumeration found 495 nonzero isotropic solutions in each of the 13 cases. Counting projective Frobenius fixed vectors by cross products for every divisor of 2h, dividing by three, and applying divisor inversion confirms every row and exactly ten distinct partitions. Separately, a different generating set and vectorized closure reproduced thirteen disjoint congruence classes of exactly the table's sizes, summing to |GL5(F2)|=9,999,360. The degree and zeta conclusions follow from those same closed-point lengths.
residual_risks: This counts the finite reduced Eckardt locus, not any infinitesimal structure of an alternative ambient parameter scheme or the zeta function of the threefold.

evidence: For the marked Klein polynomial Σ x_i²x_{i+1}, Resultary gives γ([v])=[Aᵗv^[2]] and three degree-five orbits in Fix(γ). For this permutation A, the Eckardt criterion is v^[4] proportional to A²v, hence is Fix(γ²) on the cubic.
The Klein permutation matrix has order-five C=A², identifying the unique such congruence row 1122820; C transforms by similarity under F2 congruence.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Every Gauss-fixed point in this marked example is Eckardt. Conversely over F32, γ⁵ is the identity, so Fix(γ²)=Fix(γ) over F32. This exactly credits the three 5-cycles, while Fix(γ) does not supply the fifteen 10-cycles of Fix(γ²), and the identification of the marked map does not apply to the other rows as such.

value.rationale: The exact Frobenius action on a distinguished finite cone-center locus answers a descent question not settled by geometric equivalence or rational Fano-line counts. In particular it identifies late first or full splitting (degrees five and 24), and gives the point counts over arbitrary extensions. This precise arithmetic information is useful in studying which distinguished tangent cones are available over a given finite field.
residual_risks: Only nonsingular five-variable binary Frobenius forms, not arbitrary cubic threefolds or the zeta function of the full Fano surface.
